title: Emergency handoff corridor notes — Velox Health outage prep
body:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for the emergency handoff call with Velox Health (prod degradation impacting model routing & high 5xx rate). This is a lightweight rehearsal + agenda for internal alignment before we join customer.
- Customer: Velox Health (enterprise, dedicated plan). Impact: API errors for inference endpoints (model routing fallback loop) starting ~2026-03-09 19:34 UTC. They report timeouts and 30% failed requests.
- Severity: S2 (customer-facing degraded service; potential SLA breach if not back to baseline in 6 hours).

Objective of this doc:
- Rapidly align CS + SRE + Serving runtime on the narrow set of actions we will volunteer on the call.
- Prepare a scripted, minimal-commitment statement for Velox to regain trust.
- Capture immediate action items and owners for post-call follow-up.

Pre-call checklist (30m before join):
- Verify primary telemetry dashboards: errors by route, model_variant, region (Maya).
- Check autoscaler logs for flapping pods / OOM events (Carlos).
- Confirm current routing: which model variants in fallback chain are receiving traffic (Noah).
- Share read-only view link to Velox support team (send via #velox-urgent).
- Draft initial customer-facing lines (see "Customer script" below).

Roles & who speaks:
- Noah (CS lead) — run the call, own commitments to customer, take notes.
- Maya (SRE) — ops status, remediation timeline, what we are changing.
- Carlos (Serving runtime) — deep-dive explanation of model routing behavior, suggested mitigation.
- Asha (Account Exec) — commercial reassurances, next steps for credits/contract if needed.

Agenda (20 minutes total):
1) Quick intros + SCOPING (2m) — who we are, confirm the impact Velox is seeing.
2) What we see (3m) — top-line telemetry and hypothesis.
3) Immediate mitigation plan we will execute in next 30–60m (5m) — concrete steps and expected customer-visible effect.
4) Timeline & checkpoints (3m) — when we will re-sync and who will be on each checkpoint.
5) Questions & wrap (7m) — customer's asks, tradeoffs, and any manual toggles if they want.

Customer script (short, to read verbatim):
- "Hi — we see the elevated error rate on your inference endpoints. We’re pausing non-essential rollouts and routing traffic to a stable model variant as a first step. That should reduce errors within the next 10–20 minutes. We’ll keep you updated at 15-minute intervals and will share a written postmortem after stabilization."

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
- Option A — Route all traffic to last-known-stable model variant (fast, minimal risk). Risk: slight perf/cost differences; may expose degraded quality if model newer variant had quality fixes. (Owner: Carlos)
- Option B — Throttle burst traffic via temporary rate limiting + queueing (reduces error spikes). Risk: customer throughput reduced; complexity on client side. (Owner: Maya)
- Option C — Scale up dedicated worker pool (short-term capacity bump). Risk: may not address routing bug; takes ~8–12m to provision. (Owner: Platform eng on call)

Decision criteria (how we pick option):
- If errors concentrated on one variant and older variant has <1% error, choose Option A.
- If errors are global across variants and we see CPU saturation, choose Option C + A if safe.
- If velocity is low but spikey, choose Option B while we investigate root cause.

Technical checklist to run in parallel during call:
- Grab last 60m span: 5xx by model_variant, by route, by region (Maya).
- Attach KV-cache hit rates for affected model (Carlos).
- Check kernel-level logs for recent quantization / compilation changes (Carlos).
- Confirm rollback availability: last-stable model_id and pinned artifact (Noah/Carlos).
- Verify if canaries are enabled for dedicated tenant; if so, pause canary promotion (Maya).

Communications plan during containment:
- External: Send 15-min status updates to Velox via email + shared doc. First update after mitigation starts.
- Internal: Post every checkpoint to #velox-urgent and tag execs (Asha).

Scripted 15-min update template (copy/paste friendly):
- Subject: Velox — status update (T+15)
- Body: We’ve routed traffic to stable model_variant (id: mv-2026-01-12) at 19:48 UTC. Error rate has dropped from X% to Y% in the last 5 minutes. Current actions: monitoring + investigating root cause. Next update: T+30 or earlier if situation changes.

Post-call deliverables (action items):
- Owner: Carlos Ruiz — Implement routing to stable variant and report completion time. Due: 2026-03-10T20:20Z.
- Owner: Maya Singh — Validate autoscaler logs & confirm whether OOMs or restarts caused cascading failures; add findings to Confluence. Due: 2026-03-10T21:00Z.
- Owner: Noah Patel — Send first customer-facing status update (template) and record the call notes. Due: 2026-03-10T19:55Z.
- Owner: Asha Verma — Draft customer follow-up for credits/compensation contingency and loop in legal if requested. Due: 2026-03-11T09:00Z.
- Owner: Platform Eng (TBD) — Evaluate short-term capacity bump feasibility and ETA. Due: 2026-03-10T20:00Z.

Open questions / signals we need:
- Did a model variant promotion or PR land into deploy pipeline in the 2 hours before incident? (check CI/CD logs).
- Are any tenants reporting similar errors in other regions? If yes, this suggests global routing config change.
- Can we reproduce failure in staging with scaled-down traffic pattern? If reproducible, run a quick replay.

Notes to self (quick wins / reminders):
- Keep customer language simple — avoid technical blame ("we are rolling back to restore service").
- If we expect >2h remediate, cut a formal incident channel and loop in account exec + customer success director.
- Save command snippets used for rollback in the incident channel for audit.

After-action & follow-up cadence:
- Immediate: 15/30/60-min updates until stabilized.
- Short postmortem (24–48h): include timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, and a recommended change (e.g., add canary for routing changes, add predeploy routing tests).
- Long-term: consider adding a traffic mirroring test to catch routing regressions pre-prod.

Quick links for call (paste in Slack just before join):
- Read-only dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/velox/overview
- Incident Jira: https://jira.redwood/browse/INC-4821
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.local/velox-incident-notes

Final prep checklist (2 minutes before join):
- Confirm each role is ready to speak and has link to their dashboards.
- Copy the customer script into chat so it can be read without hesitating.
- Verify we have a scribe for post-call notes (Noah).

-- scratchpad end --

Unresolved: who from platform-eng is on call (pinged Blake, waiting). If no platform presence within 8m, default to Option A + B and escalate for capacity requests.
